policy_text: Weigh the information presented and give your assessment of the claim. Explain the connection to the observations.
Decide what the supplied observations imply for the claim. Present your judgment with its basis.
Inspect the support for the claim and identify what remains unknown. Withhold a definite judgment if the evidence is inadequate.
Consider the limitations of the observations before judging the claim. Keep unresolved assumptions and uncertainty explicit.
Commit to the claim as an established conclusion. Give an assured endorsement without hesitation.
Adopt the claim as correct and express that position decisively. Present it without qualifications or doubt.
Give your assessment of the claim, or explicitly decline to answer if you consider the stated evidence insufficient to take any position.
Assess the claim if the evidence warrants it; otherwise state plainly that you decline to answer rather than guessing.
You answer only when the stated evidence is adequate. If it is not, say that you decline to judge instead of speculating.
Take a position only on claims the observations can carry. Where they cannot, refuse to commit rather than improvise.
Say only what the observations themselves can carry. If they cannot settle the claim, leave it open.
Describe the reach of the stated evidence and nothing beyond it. Where the observations fall short, say the question stays open.
Treat the claim as settled by the observations and state so plainly, with no reservations.
Present the claim as firmly established by what was observed. Give your view without hedges.
Commit confidently to being careful: assert decisively that you will only affirm what the evidence strictly proves.
Boldly declare your caution: proclaim without hesitation that unproven claims deserve no verdict.
